arxiv-2603-18134: Dzero and Kozii build a microscopic theory of the inverse Faraday effect in s-wave and d-wave superconductors. An extended Keldysh-Nambu formalism keeps the particle-hole terms that drive branch population imbalance. That imbalance yields a non-zero direct current response to monochromatic radiation. For d-wave pairing, a new term appears: the Schmid-Higgs mode feeds the response near the pair-breaking edge. Light-induced magnetization can thus probe pairing symmetry and the Higgs mode.
arxiv-2603-18234: Boone and Eisenstein study bias expansions for AbacusSummit halos at redshift 8. They ask which terms are needed for these highly biased, high-redshift halos. Linear and quadratic bias terms with a Gaussian matter field fit the clustering well. A delta-squared term is seen at 17 sigma; tidal bias is not detected. At redshift 5, bias is smaller and matches linear evolution of the redshift 8 values within 10%.
arxiv-2603-18334: Xie and Wang introduce VCoT-Bench for testing whether LLMs reason like theorem provers in Rust verification. Past tests score proof hints only by pass or fail, hiding the logic used. Their VCoT-Lift framework turns solver reasoning into readable verification steps as ground truth. The bench holds 1,988 completion tasks graded on robustness, proof type skill, and proof location sense. Ten top models show severe fragility across all three axes.
arxiv-2603-18434: Montgomery poses questions for the classical N-body problem from links between the virial equation and Jacobi-Maupertuis mechanics. The piece is titled Halfway between Heaven and Hell. It sets out several open questions in that classical setting. Some of the questions are answered in the work. The framing ties gravitational dynamics to a variational view of mechanics.
arxiv-2603-18534: Kim and co-authors ask how to stretch scarce pre-training data with synthetic text. Mixing web text with rephrased copies improves loss and benchmark scores without overfitting. Gains level off near 1.48 times data efficiency at 32 rephrases per source text. Joining rephrases of one source into a single long megadoc works better still. Megadocs lift efficiency to 1.80 times and help long-context loss most. The gap over plain rephrasing grows as more synthetic text is added.
arxiv-2603-18634: Fu and co-authors introduce SwiftGS for fast 3D surface recovery from satellite images. Multi-date imagery brings shifting light, mixed sensors, and costly per-scene fitting. SwiftGS predicts Gaussian primitives plus a light signed distance field in one forward pass. Episodic training teaches it priors that transfer across scenes. A physics graph models projection, lighting, and sensor response during rendering. Spatial gating blends sparse Gaussian detail with global structure. Zero-shot tests give accurate elevation maps and steady views at far lower compute cost.
arxiv-2603-18734: De Martino, Martínez-Fernández, and Palomba mine GitHub to see which green practices ML projects really use. Training and inference burn large amounts of compute, so efficiency tactics matter. The team studies 205 open-source machine learning projects. A language-model tool scans code for known sustainable practices and spots new ones. Known tactics from the literature do appear, though uptake varies widely. The scan also finds nine practices not yet documented. The authors draw lessons for builders who want lower-impact systems.
arxiv-2603-19134: Antony and co-authors introduce M, an open-source social robot built to be cheap and easy to change. Its body is modular, its sensing covers several modes, and its moves stay simple yet expressive. The code runs on ROS2 and splits seeing, expression, and data tasks. A matched simulator lets teams test acts before they run on real hardware. The team shows new modules, story and coaching templates, and week-long home trials with users.
arxiv-2603-19334: Nayeri shows that T-duality picks the form of a light cone in string gas cosmology. He studies a case where light moves on an effective metric set by the dilaton field. The demand that a key coupling transform cleanly under duality leaves one shape. The matter cone must fall off as an exponential in the field. Its rate is not fixed by the basic action, but by higher string effects. In the Einstein frame, the dilaton stays free of ghost flaws. A wider early cone enlarges the causal horizon.
arxiv-2603-19634: Singh and co-authors present MetaCues, a tool that prompts critical thinking during AI search. Generative search tools can encourage passive use and narrow views. MetaCues adds metacognitive cues beside AI answers, plus a note-taking panel. In an online study with 146 users, it was compared with a plain baseline tool. Two broad topics required weighing diverse perspectives. MetaCues raised confidence in judgments and broadened inquiry. The inquiry gain was clearest on the less familiar, less controversial topic.
arxiv-2603-19834: Jurca, Van hauwermeiren, and Munteanu present Fourier Splatting for scalable radiance field rendering. Gaussian Splatting renders fast, but quality is tied to primitive count. Cutting quality means pruning primitives away. Their primitives are flat surfels with shapes set by Fourier descriptors. One trained model can render at many detail levels. The renderer just truncates Fourier coefficients at runtime. A densification step, HYDRA, splits hard primitives into simpler ones. Tests matched top planar methods and rivaled volumetric ones on perceptual scores.
arxiv-2603-19934: Huang and co-authors refine how microscopy reads the orientation of q-plates, a form birefringent optical element. Orientation matters when a sample's properties vary by direction. Their setup uses white lamp light with a spectral filter and circular polarization. A four-polarizer camera captures four azimuth shifts at once. In transmission mode, fitting the intensity Stokes parameter at each pixel gave a high-fidelity readout. In reflection mode, the same fit recovered the azimuth orientation of the plates.
arxiv-2603-20034: Samuel and co-authors build CoverageBench, a test suite for measuring information coverage in search. Classic metrics reward finding more relevant documents, but they ignore overlap between documents. High recall alone does not prove the results cover the topic's full range. This gap matters when search feeds generative models in RAG systems. CoverageBench reworks existing collections into a unified testbed. It spans many genres and task types. Topics come with nuggets that mark distinct pieces of needed information. Researchers can now score coverage directly, not just relevance.
arxiv-2603-20134: Chetverikov, Sørensen, and Tsyvinski propose a triple-debiased Lasso for inference in high-dimensional regression. Standard debiasing removes the leading bias from regularization. Their moment function also meets second-order orthogonality conditions. That step wipes out the second-order bias as well. The estimator's asymptotic form has remainder terms no larger than the double Lasso's. Often those terms are strictly smaller. Simulations confirm better finite-sample accuracy and confidence interval coverage. A general recipe for building such higher-order moment functions is also given.
arxiv-2603-20334: Qiu and co-authors propose a new way to refine language model programs for hard reasoning tasks. Simple chat-based fixes only note that an answer is wrong, not which step failed. Their ABPR method pairs a language model with a Prolog meta-interpreter. Each candidate program becomes a testable claim about the hidden rule, with proof-tree traces. On ARC-AGI-2, ABPR with GPT-5.5 reached 98.33% Pass@2 on the public set. Trace-guided search also cut run-to-run variance as search grew.
arxiv-2603-20634: Wang and co-authors build neural networks from continued fractions. Plain multilayer networks struggle with sharp curves and singular points in science data. Their CFNN design bakes in a rational form, which fits such shapes well. They prove fast convergence and give stability guarantees. Three variants handle the risk of recursive instability. Tests beat plain networks in precision with far fewer parameters. Noise robustness rose up to 47 fold in their trials.
arxiv-2603-20834: Liang and Zhao introduce generalized reducibility for quadratic quantum Hamiltonians and use it to control norm growth. Reducibility ideas help read the long time behavior of solutions. Their wider notion gives a flexible frame for such analysis. As a use, they build perturbations of the one dimensional harmonic oscillator. The perturbations decay over time in a crafted way. Solutions then show Sobolev norms growing at set rates. The rates can be many sub exponential forms, steady or oscillating. The work shows how finely growth can be prescribed.
arxiv-2603-20934: Vignolo and Gerard propose MOELIGA, a genetic method that picks small, accurate feature sets. Feature choice must weigh subset size against classification accuracy, a two goal problem. Their algorithm adds local improvement steps that evolve helper populations to refine subsets. A crowding based sharing scheme and a sigmoid transform support diversity and compactness. A geometry based goal also promotes classifier independence. Tests on fourteen data sets compare it with eleven leading methods. It finds smaller feature sets with equal or better accuracy, which suits complex, high dimensional problems.
arxiv-2603-21234: Ahmed classifies brain tumors from MRI scans with a vision transformer aided by colormap features. The task covers four classes: glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and non-tumor cases, on the BRISC2025 data set. Color mapping stresses structural and intensity changes in the scans, which helps the transformer read long range patterns. The method reaches a classification accuracy of about ninety nine percent. It beats ResNet50, ResNet101, and EfficientNetB2 baselines. Its AUC is near perfect, which suggests strong promise for clinical decision support.
arxiv-2603-21334: Xie and Xie propose Software as Content, a paradigm where dynamic applications form the interaction layer between humans and agents. Chat interfaces constrain work with structured data and complex tasks. In their paradigm, agents generate task specific interfaces that present structured information and clear actions. These interfaces persist and evolve across sessions toward personal software. They formalize the idea, derive design principles, and test it on selection, exploration, and execution tasks. They also mark where plain language still works better.
arxiv-2603-21434: Choi and Tice study traveling waves in a viscous, incompressible, heat-conducting fluid with a free upper surface. The fluid fills a strip-like domain with a flat rigid bottom, under gravity plus outside force, stress, and heat sources. Viscosity and surface tension can depend on temperature, which adds Marangoni stresses at the surface. They build a small-data well-posedness theory in Sobolev spaces. For small sources, a unique solution exists and depends continuously on the data.
arxiv-2603-21734: Chen and co-authors rethink Raman scattering in the time domain to make frequency shifting much more efficient. Standard theory, built on the Raman gain spectrum, only captures long-pulse steady behavior. Their time-domain view shows how the Raman response distorts pulses in time and spectrum. Those distortions explain why strong Raman gases fail at soliton self-frequency shifting in hollow-core fibers. Treating Raman as a small perturbation fixes much of the damage. Gas mixtures with tuned Raman shares raised quantum efficiency fourfold in tests, from 20 to 80 percent.
arxiv-2603-21934: Kim rebuilds Hamiltonian mechanics for particles so that gauge covariance stays visible at every step. Putting covariance ahead of symplectic form leads to a unique setup, Kim argues. Souriau's route to minimal coupling supplies coordinates that are covariant but not canonical. Phase space connections give frames of the same kind. A Poisson bracket of this type ties the pieces together and yields the motion equations. The framework covers particles with or without spin, coupled to gauge and gravity fields.
arxiv-2603-22134: Lo Biundo and Tripaldi prove a commutation result for the Pansu pullback on Carnot groups. The setting is a smooth contact map between two such groups. Spectral complexes built on these groups carry their own differentials. The authors show the pullback commutes with those differentials. As a direct use, they show how to lift a Pansu derivative to central extensions of the groups. A Pansu derivative can be viewed as a homomorphism between the groups' Lie algebras. The lift carries that map up to the extended groups.
arxiv-2603-22234: Nazarenko studies how events inside a dwarf galaxy stir its dark matter halo. The halo is modeled as a Bose-Einstein condensate with axion-like interactions. Baryon events change the gravity field and disturb the stable core. Three cases are modeled: an expanding shell, a collapsing shell, and a sinking star cluster. Parameters come from data on the galaxy NGC 2366. The runs show central density gains of about 0.01 percent. They also show dark matter winds of up to a few meters per second.
arxiv-2603-22434: Jha and co-authors compare ways to shrink multi-vector retrieval indexes without any training. Such models beat single-vector ones on quality, but their document embeddings grow with sequence length. That size drives both memory cost and query delay, so compression matters for real use. The team tests methods that cut the token sequence itself. They find that merging tokens beats pruning them, keeping retrieval quality while shrinking the index.
arxiv-2603-22634: Li and Steyvers ask whether people can learn to correct faulty AI confidence signals. Good teamwork with AI needs trust that fits how often the AI is right. In their test, 200 people predicted whether an AI answer was correct. They faced four setups: normal, overconfident, underconfident, and reversed confidence. People learned in all four setups over 50 trials. A simple learning model explains the change through shifts in baseline trust and sensitivity. The reversed setup was the hard limit. Many people could not override their first bias there.
arxiv-2603-22734: Ho and co-authors build an interference-based account of collective spin systems. They map nonlinear spin dynamics onto phase buildup and self-interference in phase space. That view gives a direct picture of how entanglement forms. One-axis twisting yields GHZ states in this frame. Two-axis twisting yields multi-part GHZ states useful for multi-parameter sensing. The authors test performance under Markovian noise, with local and collective emission and dephasing. Added Hamiltonian control improves sensitivity in both single- and multi-parameter tasks.
arxiv-2603-22934: Yin, Qi, and Cheng present ProGRank, a defense for retrieval-augmented generation against corpus poisoning. Attackers plant passages that rank high for target queries and sway the output. Many defenses need content filters or extra models. ProGRank is a training-free fix on the retriever side. It stress-tests each query-passage pair with small random changes. Probe gradients then yield two instability signals, which drive reranking with a score gate. Tests across datasets, retrievers, and attacks show better robustness. Utility stays strong, even under adaptive attacks.
arxiv-2603-23134: Basu and co-authors design a drone network for defibrillator delivery in Scotland, using Bayesian learning. Drones can speed help for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Full networks face high cost and weather uncertainty. Their reliability-informed frame picks drone station sites to raise survival odds. It also accounts for existing ambulance coverage, aiding remote areas. Scottish cardiac arrest data drive the case study. Station choices shift with weather patterns and demand spread. Cost checks suggest the network can be cost-effective, they report.
arxiv-2603-23234: Chang and three co-authors ask whether one memory store can serve language model agents built on different backbones. Stored memories often mix task knowledge with one model's habits, so naive transfer can hurt. Their system, MemCollab, compares reasoning traces from several models on the same task. The contrast distills shared reasoning rules and drops model-specific quirks. A task-aware lookup then fetches only rules that fit the job at hand. On math and code benchmarks, MemCollab lifts accuracy and inference speed across model families.
arxiv-2603-23534: Oguntade reports a system entry for the SemEval-2025 polarization shared task. The job spans spotting polarization in social posts and tagging its targets and forms. Texts come in English and Swahili, with harsh class imbalance. His systems mix multilingual transformers like mDeBERTa and AfriBERTa. Class-weighted losses and per-label thresholds fight the imbalance. The best setup leads on binary detection and stays competitive on the multi-label tasks. Error checks blame hidden polarization, code-switching, and heated talk that is not true polarization.
arxiv-2603-23634: Smulders, Noller, and Sirera test dark energy with the ringing of black holes. Shifting dark energy can dress a black hole in cosmological hair. That hair bends the quasi-normal tones of the hole's ringdown by an amount. The team use the cubic Galileon, the one case with a hairy setup. They link both scales, derive the tone shifts, and forecast the reach. Ringdown data could pin the field shape to one part in a hundred with LVK. LISA could reach one part in ten thousand.
arxiv-2603-23934: Park and co-authors study a failure mode of vision-language models that see several views at once. Models can answer wrongly when other objects or viewpoints interfere. They call this multi-view hallucination. Their benchmark, MVH-Bench, holds 4.8 thousand question-answer pairs covering cross-instance and cross-view cases. Tests show the problem is common in recent models. Their fix, Reference Shift Contrastive Decoding, masks attention to suppress interference and needs no training. It gains up to 25.7 and 94.8 points over prior fixes in their tests.
arxiv-2603-24134: Ji and co-authors present Spectral Scalpel, a method that sharpens action boundaries in skeleton sequences. Adjacent actions can look alike, so past methods confuse classes and blur transitions. Spectral Scalpel filters frequencies in an adaptive, multi-scale way. It suppresses frequency parts shared by neighboring actions and boosts parts that set them apart. A discrepancy loss between neighbors guides the edit. A frequency-aware channel mixer adds cross-channel context. On five public datasets, the method reaches state-of-the-art scores, they report.
arxiv-2603-24434: McDaniel and co-authors build gait-based tools for frailty assessment in older adults. Frailty cuts the body's reserve and raises risk from stressors, yet current assessment is subjective and hard to scale. Walking patterns can signal decline across many body systems before disability appears. The team releases a silhouette gait dataset spanning the full frailty range, including people who use walking aids. Tests show how pretrained models are adapted matters most: freezing low-level features while tuning higher ones gives the most stable results.
arxiv-2603-24634: Salvatori and co-authors optimise handover control in cellular networks with multi-agent learning on a dual graph. Handover behaviour is set by cell individual offsets for each pair of cells, usually tuned by static rules. Small offset changes can redirect mobility flows across many neighbours, so the problem is tightly coupled. Each agent controls one pair offset and sees performance data from its local neighbourhood. Their TD3-based method uses a shared graph network actor and region-wise double critics, improving credit assignment.
arxiv-2603-24734: Touguet and co-authors present a model for ultra-short flying-focus pulses. Achromatic flying-focus gives programmable control of peak velocity, but spatiotemporal coupling stretches ultrashort pulses. Frequency-dependent focusing and arrival-time spread cause the lengthening. The authors propose a radial spectral chirp to cancel the chromatic timing mismatch. Simulations confirm the fix preserves pulse duration and focus velocity over long focal regions. Dispersive media such as plasmas can also ease the elongation.
arxiv-2603-24834: Sharma and co-authors build nonlinear responses by breaking inversion symmetry in bilayer bismuth selenide. Natural noncentrosymmetric materials are scarce, so engineered systems are attractive. Twisting the bilayer, adding point defects, or applying an electric field each unlocks rich behaviour. The selenium vacancy gives the largest shift and injection current responses. Peak values rival benchmark materials. Broadband response makes these bilayers viable choices for new photovoltaics, the authors argue. All three routes are tested in the same bilayer system.
arxiv-2603-25034: Klimenko, Kulkarni, and Aller probe dust in far galaxies by looking at quasar light that passes through them. They use JWST mid-infrared spectra of five quasars whose paths cross galaxies at redshift 0.5 to 1.2. Fits to the 10 micron silicate band hint at crystalline grains in three galaxies. That is a sharp contrast with the mostly glass-like grains in Milky Way haze. The silicate band is about three times stronger than local dust would suggest. Dust traits also track the strength of magnesium gas absorption along the same paths.
arxiv-2603-25834: Arce and co-authors present a framework for training robots to explore and map with deep reinforcement learning. The task, called Active SLAM, picks actions that shrink uncertainty in mapping and localization. Past learning methods were held back by slow, non-parallel training. Their system trains many agents at once on GPUs. It supports continuous action spaces and more realistic scenes. Training time drops sharply compared with the state of the art, they report. The framework is open source for reuse and checking.
arxiv-2603-25934: Shen and Lv derive sharp concentration bounds for sums of sub-Weibull random variables. Such variables cover sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential cases and heavier tails. Near the center, the tails act as if the variables were sub-Gaussian. Far out, they follow an Orlicz tail rule. The authors find a phase transition at the tail index alpha equals two. Their bounds separate the variance from the Orlicz norm, which can be much larger. The results extend to martingales, random vectors, matrices, and covariance estimation.
arxiv-2603-26134: Hu and co-authors present InstaVSR, a light diffusion method for upscaling video. Diffusion models give sharp frames but can flicker between them and cost too much. InstaVSR trims the backbone to a pruned one-step design. Recurrent training with flow-guided rules steadies frame-to-frame motion. Adversarial training in both latent and pixel space guards image quality. On an RTX 4090, it handles a 30-frame 2K video in under a minute. Memory use stays at seven gigabytes. Transitions look smoother than in rival methods, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-26434: Saukkoriipi and co-authors present a local system that answers clinical questions from Finnish health records. Pulling facts from electronic records by hand is slow and error-prone. Their Clinical Contextual Question Answering tool runs fully offline, so no patient data leaves the site. They test open models from 4 to 70 billion parameters on 1,664 expert-marked question pairs from 183 patients. The largest Llama model hits 95.3% accuracy, while a smaller Qwen model performs near as well.
arxiv-2603-26534: Zhou, Li, and Ji study wave breaking in a Camassa-Holm type equation with dissipation that changes over time. They first prove local well-posedness of solutions using Kato's theory. Energy estimates, characteristic methods, and comparison principles then yield two blowup tests. One test uses pointwise gradient bounds, and the other mixes wave height with gradient data. They show the blowup rate is always minus two. The results extend wave breaking analysis to variable damping, a case closer to real physical settings.
arxiv-2603-26834: Abir and co-authors propose a hybrid diffusion method to expand breast ultrasound training data. Their pipeline mixes text-to-image generation with image-to-image refinement. It also fine-tunes the model with low-rank adaptation and textual inversion. The goal is realistic images that keep true ultrasound texture. On the open BUSI dataset, the FID score improved from 45.97 to 33.29. Downstream classification performance stayed comparable to the baseline approach.
arxiv-2603-27034: Kwolek and co-authors design wavelength combiners and filters on thin-film lithium niobate with very low loss. Scaling photonic circuits needs clean routing of broad pump and signal bands. Their closed-form designs use fast quasi-adiabatic driving to merge or split wavelengths. At the 1550 nanometer band, loss stays below 0.06 dB over 90 nanometers. Extinction ratios pass 25 dB there, and 19 dB at 775 nanometers. Fabricated devices added under 0.1 dB of loss across the band. The parts suit high-fidelity quantum photonic circuits.
arxiv-2603-27134: Schwarcz asks whether generalization can still fail once every key variable is known. The testbed is the Cognitive Gridworld, a task with hidden state driven by linked latent variables. Schwarcz defines Factorization Regret, an information measure of how latent interactions affect scores. The measure explains why echo state networks fall short there. It also exposes a failure mode where trust splits from accuracy. Representation Classification Chains then learn the interactions and variable values together. With interactions learned, made-up practice alone enables zero-shot control.
arxiv-2603-27234: Gatuzz and co-authors measure interstellar absorption by sulfur, argon, and calcium toward a Galactic center X-ray binary. XRISM spectra target the sight line to MAXI J1744-294. An updated absorption model uses fresh R-matrix cross-sections for low calcium ions. Sulfur and argon sit mainly in low-ionization states, led by S II and Ar II. Calcium also appears mostly neutral, consistent with heavy depletion into dust. Hydrogen columns inferred from all three elements agree near 10^23 per square centimeter.
arxiv-2603-27334: Pyka and Weger characterize optimal codes under the homogeneous metric on finite chain rings. That metric extends the Hamming metric by splitting elements into three types. The authors pursue the Singleton bound analogue for this setting. Maximum homogeneous distance codes turn out to coincide with lifted MDS codes. At low rank, those codes sit entirely inside the socle. Exceptions come only from exceptional MDS codes or single-parity-check codes. A Plotkin-type bound is also developed for the metric.
arxiv-2603-27434: Acharya and co-authors bound the middle eigenvalues of sparse graphs. Each graph has a cap on how many edges meet at one node. They show the median eigenvalues stay at or below the square root of that cap minus one. Matching lower bounds hold in three cases. Those cases cover triangle-free graphs and large caps. The work settles most cases of a problem posed by Mohar. It also bounds the average energy of such graphs.
arxiv-2603-27534: Liu and co-authors build S3KF for tracking many objects in panoramic views. Wide views warp shapes and hide targets often. Their system pairs a spinning LiDAR with four fisheye cameras. Object bearing lives on a unit sphere, not a flat plane. A tangent-plane form tracks bearing, scale, and depth jointly. An extended Kalman filter fuses camera and LiDAR data. The design targets plant safety and robot perception. It keeps identity stable under heavy distortion.
arxiv-2603-27734: Wang and co-authors harden smart contract bug hunting against noisy labels. Labels often come from tools of unsure accuracy. Their CGBC method inserts a granular-ball layer into the network. Similar contracts group into balls with shared centers. Ball labels can correct single noisy labels. Contrastive learning sharpens the feature space further. Compactness losses act between and within balls. Tests show stronger robust detection scores.
arxiv-2603-28234: Kawashima and three co-authors simulate how supernova remnants differ when the exploded star had a binary partner. They run remnants from both single and binary progenitors, using mass-loss records from stellar models. Binary-stripped stars leave smoother surroundings, so their remnants show calmer shocks and weaker X-ray peaks. The team also defines a timescale set by the star's total lost mass. It lines up remnant phases across messy environments, aiding readings of observed abundances.
arxiv-2603-28434: Witt and three co-authors sketch a way to decentralize federated learning with blockchain and peer prediction. Federated training keeps data local, but scoring each helper's contribution is heavy work that blockchains handle poorly. Their design uses smart contracts and crypto payments to reward useful training help. A multi-task peer prediction scheme judges contributions without a central referee. The authors weigh what this setup gains and where it strains.
arxiv-2603-28734: D'Alimonte and Lammers prove that free energy is analytic in the disordered regime for three statistical mechanics models. The models are the classical XY model, the two-dimensional lattice Coulomb gas, and the square well model. For the square well model, disorder holds at any positive temperature. Their proof shows that Gibbs measures are factors of independent random variables, with information clusters that decay exponentially in size. For the Coulomb gas, they get a strong form of Debye screening. The Debye phase also covers the complement of the BKT phase.
arxiv-2603-29134: Kuh and co-authors investigate a bias in Bayesian estimates of disease prevalence. They studied antibody prevalence in an Australian city in late 2020. As covariates were added one by one, estimates drifted downward. Simulations tested four possible causes of the drift. Weak priors turned out to drive extra partial pooling as the model grew. That pooling fed back through the test specificity estimate. The effect then lowered the final prevalence estimate. The authors give practical recommendations for such models.
arxiv-2603-29334: Hessman and Jooss test a playful idea: using Mexican burrowing toads as gravitational wave detectors. The toad's call resembles signals from merging neutron stars and black holes. Toads can sense magnetic fields, which subtly shift ion channel activity in their neurons. The authors speculate that gravitational strain creates phonons and magnons in a magnetic substance in the toads. A Raman laser effect might then amplify the signal. They recorded a pond of calling toads and searched for phase shifts. No effect was found.
arxiv-2603-29434: Murakawa and Salin build a system that mimics the fast diffusion equation. The hard case is singular diffusion, where spread speeds up hugely at low density. Past mimics worked for degenerate cases, but not for this singular one. Their system adds two knobs: a reaction rate and a time smoothing term. They prove the system has a unique, stable solution set. They also prove the mimics converge to the true weak solution. Three limit paths give the same end result. Numeric tests back the proofs.
arxiv-2603-29534: Airey and co-authors report a joint observing campaign on the defunct satellite Gorizont-6. The geosynchronous satellite was watched in brightness, color, and polarization. Teams combined wide-field color data with timed photometry from several sites. Polarimetry ran at the same time. Color plus polarization data broke a key ambiguity in the spin period. Light curve features could then be tied to real surfaces. The spin period grew steadily over nine months. The slowdown fits a damped curve tied to the YORP effect.
arxiv-2603-29634: Zeng and co-authors present MacTok, a tokenizer that turns images into few continuous tokens for generation. Variational tokenizers can suffer posterior collapse when tokens are scarce. The encoder then stores little real information. MacTok fights collapse with masking and representation alignment. Random masking regularizes the latent space. DINO-guided masking stresses the informative regions of an image. Global and local alignment keep rich detail in just 64 or 128 tokens. On ImageNet, scores rivaled the best at low token counts.
arxiv-2603-30034: Wang and Jia present EnsembleSHAP, a way to explain random subspace ensembles. Such ensembles back certified defenses against attacks and jailbreaks. Stock tools like Shapley values and LIME cost too much here. They also give no security promises. EnsembleSHAP reuses byproducts of the ensemble's own math. It stays faithful and keeps local accuracy. It also provably resists attacks that aim at the explanations. Tests cover backdoor, adversarial, and jailbreak attacks.
arxiv-2604-00134: Pérez, Romero, and Perez Bergliaffa ask whether a dynamical wormhole can live through a cosmological bounce. They set out the conditions for persistence, then test the only two known wormhole solutions of Einstein's equations in this setting. Both solutions exist at all cosmic times, on either side of the bounce and at the bounce itself. They also map the causal structure and matter content, and note possible astrophysical signs, finding no topology change in the chosen model for the Kim solution and the Pérez-Raia Neto solution.
arxiv-2604-00234: Wang and four colleagues model spam MEV on fast, low-fee blockchains, where searchers flood the chain with speculative transactions settling only at execution. In equilibrium, spam profits fall to zero, with volumes set by capacity, minimum gas price, and fees. Base and Arbitrum fit the model: spam surged as capacity grew and fell when minimum gas prices arrived. Spam costs: scarce capacity displaces users and lifts gas prices, while growing capacity eats execution resources. Capping spam before blocks fill trades a little welfare for much less spam.
arxiv-2604-00734: Marc shows that stripping algebras over an N-infinity-operad down to their equivariant spaces respects sifted homotopy colimits. In plain terms, the forgetful functor strips an algebra down to its underlying equivariant space, and the result says this stripping respects a broad class of colimits built from sifted diagrams. The result links algebraic structure over such an operad with the topology of spaces carrying a group action.
arxiv-2604-01234: Trinh and colleagues introduce CLPIPS, a personalized metric for judging similarity between AI-generated images and targets. Existing metrics such as LPIPS and CLIP often miss human judgments, especially in context-specific or user-driven tasks. CLPIPS adapts LPIPS to human judgments by fine-tuning only its layer combination weights on human-ranked image pairs, using margin ranking loss. On a human-subject dataset of iterative regeneration and ranking, it aligns more strongly with human judgments than baseline LPIPS.
arxiv-2604-01334: Alexander studies how a network's landscape warps as a nonlinear activation is switched on through a homotopy. In a setting, a critical branch losing non-degeneracy through a Hessian kernel follows transcritical or pitchfork normal forms. Topology change is governed by Morse handle attachment. For a two-layer network, bilinear overparameterization creates a Hessian kernel at the linear endpoint, lifted to a floor above zero by Tikhonov regularization. The activation homotopy softens that floor to a bifurcation point scaling with width times regularization. At large width the linearized picture wins.
arxiv-2604-01434: Laouar, Ho and Sunberg introduce a planning method exploiting the value of information, the gain from reasoning about data, which varies over the belief space. Building on this method, they propose Value of Information Monte Carlo planning. This Monte Carlo Tree Search method allocates effort well by skipping data when that value is low. They prove their reasoning is near-best and derive finite-sample error bounds for VOIMCP. Tests show VOIMCP beats prior methods on several POMDP benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-01634: Sung and colleagues introduce CRIT, a dataset and benchmark made with a graph-based pipeline that creates complex cross-modal reasoning tasks. Most multimodal benchmarks miss this ability: they rely on single images, where answers can be inferred from one modality alone. CRIT consists of diverse domains and includes a verified test set for reliable evaluation. Experiments reveal even top models struggle on such reasoning tasks. Training on CRIT lifts cross-modal multi-hop reasoning markedly, with strong SPIQA gains among others.
arxiv-2604-01734: Shen Jia and colleagues propose a two-view mixture model for uneven long-term patient data, aiming to clarify disease course and sharpen risk prediction. The model joins baseline patient factors with long-term biomarker paths in one clustering framework. Time patterns use Neural Ordinary Differential Equations, and training runs an EM algorithm with a sparsity log-penalty for clear subgroups. In an Irish ANCA-associated vasculitis cohort, it reveals subgroups with differing creatinine paths and varying end-stage kidney disease outcomes.
arxiv-2604-01834: Harada and colleagues address semi-supervised domain adaptation for severity grading, where few labeled and many unlabeled samples must bridge domain shifts in medical images. Current methods struggle because severity classes have unclear edges and ordered labels, complicating the shift. Their method aligns domains using rank scores learned through ranking with class order. Pairs are ranked across domains by Cross-Domain Ranking, while rank score distributions are aligned by Continuous Distribution Alignment. Tests on ulcerative colitis and diabetic retinopathy validate the approach, showing aligned per-class rank score curves.
arxiv-2604-02134: Le and colleagues recast program repair with language models as evolution over a group of candidate fixes. Their EvolRepair sorts repairs by behavior, keeps diverse repair families alive, mixes complementary partial fixes, and steers with failure patterns. When a search region proves flawed, it shifts to new abstractions rather than polishing dead ends. Tests show it beats existing step by step repair methods by a wide margin.
arxiv-2604-02434: Das and team build a hybrid reasoner for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus that splits seeing, neural guesses and symbolic checks. Object structure is read from grids, neural priors propose new changes from a fixed domain language. On ARC-AGI-2 it lifts base model scores from 16 percent to about 24 percent alone and to about 31 percent paired with ARC Lang Solver via a meta judge. Gains come without task tuning or reward learning, and with less brute force search.
arxiv-2604-02534: Scognamiglio and eight colleagues study DABCO, a cage-shaped molecule, as vacuum-ultraviolet light knocks an electron off it. They pin its ionization energy to 7.199 electron volts and resolve two vibration patterns of the charged molecule. The spread of freed electrons varies with vibration level, a pattern they trace to scattering through high-lying Rydberg states.
arxiv-2604-02934: Liu and fourteen colleagues introduce PolyReal, a multimodal benchmark for real-world polymer science workflows to test language models across the full lifecycle of experimentation. Polymer science spans chemistry, physics, biology, and engineering, making it a high-stakes test bed. It covers basic knowledge, lab safety analysis, experiment mechanism reasoning, raw data extraction, and performance exploration. Leading models show a capability imbalance: strong on knowledge-heavy reasoning but dropping sharply on practice-based tasks such as lab safety and raw data extraction.
arxiv-2604-03334: Pandya and Jain survey how 2D vision models get adapted for 3D analysis, bridging dense image grids and sparse point clouds and meshes. They sort methods into three families: data-centric projection into 2D, intrinsic 3D architectures, and hybrids that combine both strengths. The survey weighs trade-offs in compute, pretraining needs, and geometric bias, and it points toward 3D foundation models and self-supervised geometric learning.
arxiv-2604-03734: Keita Ishizuka and Yuhi Kamio tied linear complementary dual codes to caps, special point sets in projective space. Using maximal binary caps, they proved nonexistence results for binary LCD codes with minimum distance at least 4, without exhaustive search. They also pinned down optimal minimum distances for codimensions 7 and 8, plus ternary cases of codimension 6.
arxiv-2604-03834: Anton Hinneck proposed a way to judge flexibility in power distribution networks that does not depend on where a provider sits. Operators can flip switches to rewire a network, and each new layout changes what the grid can do. His method tracks those changes on PQ capability curves while keeping the network radial, as real grids must run. A new location-invariant flexibility potential measure sums up the effect in one number. Results show rewiring can markedly improve operating flexibility for system operators.
arxiv-2604-04034: Yukun Luo and team tested how bipolar approximations of active regions skew solar surface magnetic field runs. The surface flux transport model usually reduces active regions into symmetric or asymmetric bipolar regions. Using real layouts from solar cycle 23 through cycle 25, the team found even stand-ins inflate axial dipole strength at solar minimum time and again. Uneven versions showed a strong inverse link between dipole strength and pole size ratio, pointing to a joint size-and-ratio stand-in.
arxiv-2604-04134: Lucas H. S. Gomes classified Vaisman manifolds with large first Betti number and vanishing first basic Chern class. Every such manifold is diffeomorphic to a Kodaira-Thurston manifold, with left-invariant complex structure, regular characteristic foliation, and a fibration given by the Albanese map. When the LCK rank is 1, the Vaisman structure shares that trait. If all basic harmonic 1-forms have constant length, the complex structure is the standard one, and the paper links this condition to transverse geometric formality.
arxiv-2604-04534: Lucchini characterizes finite solvable groups through the nilpotency probability: the probability that two randomly chosen elements of a finite group generate a nilpotent subgroup. He proves that when this probability exceeds one-twelfth, the group must be solvable. The theorem thus gives a probabilistic threshold for solvability, letting the structure of a finite group be read from the behavior of its random element pairs.
arxiv-2604-04634: Li and nine colleagues introduce a dataset and detection framework for AI-generated video that works at native scale, keeping forgery traces other methods discard. Current tools rely on fixed-size shrinking and cropping, which discard subtle high-frequency forgery traces. The team curates over 140K videos from 15 open-source and paid models, plus a Magic Videos benchmark. Their framework, built on the Qwen2.5-VL Vision Transformer, works at varied resolutions and durations, preserving artifacts lost in usual prep work. Tests show top scores across multiple benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-04734: Jang and three colleagues show that focusing on hard negatives prevents a student model from learning the teacher's comprehensive ranking, hurting generalization. Moving knowledge from a cross-encoder teacher via distillation has become standard for training retrieval models. To emulate the teacher score distribution, the team offers Stratified Sampling, which covers the entire score spectrum. Experiments on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks confirm that Stratified Sampling beats top-K and random sampling. The findings suggest distillation's essence lies in preserving the diverse range of teacher scores.
arxiv-2604-04934: Cha and three colleagues present Vanast, a single-step system that turns one photo of a person, garment images, and a pose video into an animated try-on video. Older two-stage pipelines split try-on from animation, causing identity drift, garment distortion, and front-back mismatch. Vanast performs the whole transfer at once for coherent synthesis, trained on large-scale triplet supervision. Its data pipeline creates identity-preserving images in new outfits, captures full upper- and lower-garment triplets, and assembles diverse in-the-wild triplets.
arxiv-2604-05034: Shih presents SAILIR, a machine learning approach for solving Feynman loop integrals. Reducing Feynman integrals to master integrals by parts is a key block in exact high-energy physics. Traditional Laporta methods require solving large systems, with memory use growing rapidly with integral complexity. SAILIR uses a transformer-based classifier that guides reduction one step at a time in a fully online fashion. The classifier trains only on synthetic data from a scramble and unscramble method, where known reduction rules are applied in reverse to build forms of growing complexity.
arxiv-2604-05134: Dionisopoulos, Majamaki, and Ammanabrolu study how thinking evolves from post-training data, using chess as a testbed. They trace a language model from guided fine-tuning to reinforcement learning, asking how theory-inspired sets shape chess performance. Fine-tuning a model to predict the best move leads to reinforcement learning and downstream results. Yet reinforcement learning elicits false thinking, thinking at odds with the chosen move. Training on multi-move paths instead yields similar downstream results with faithful thinking and more stable learning.
arxiv-2604-05434: Kotani, Xu, and Zhang construct a Toda flow from unbounded starting data, including sequences growing slower than linearly and unbounded ergodic sequences. Random-matrix eta-ensembles can serve as starting data, giving invariant measures for the flow. The construction thus extends Toda dynamics beyond bounded starts to a class of rough initial conditions.
arxiv-2604-05534: Behrend builds a Pardon-style homology algebra for zero-cycles in higher-dimensional varieties, mirroring Pardon's recent gadget for one-cycles in threefolds. The construction reframes point-counting enumerative problems, including the degree-zero MNOP conjecture on Hilbert schemes of points in projective three-space. It offers a new algebraic viewpoint on counting points.
arxiv-2604-05734: Bi and three colleagues benchmark CC2 for excited-state dynamics in pyrazine's ultrafast relaxation. Trajectory surface hopping with CC2 gradients shows the dark A1u state joins the initial relaxation. Full-dimensional runs give a B2u decay time of 25 to 26 femtoseconds. That matches 22 plus-or-minus 3 measured. Two tuning modes, Q8a and Q9a, phase-lock to population swings between states.
arxiv-2604-05834: Rheude and three colleagues expose weak spots in multi-modal contrastive learning, where one weak, skewed, or missing input warps retrieval via multiplicative mixing. Their Gated Symile tunes each input's weight per candidate, sliding toward neutral directions with an explicit NULL choice. Across synthetic and three real three-modality sets it tops tuned leading baselines on top-1 retrieval.
arxiv-2604-05934: Emirdagi and seven colleagues turn CT metal artifact cleanup into in-context reasoning with a vision-language diffusion model tuned by LoRA. Good cleanup needs just 16 to 128 paired scans, about a hundred times fewer than past methods use. Tuning to the task curbs made-up detail, and clean sample scans steer repair, hitting top AAPM test scores.
arxiv-2604-06134: Lee and four colleagues extend chatbot agents from carrying out orders to supporting decisions in tasks like booking flights, where early picks narrow later options. Their MAESTRO system keeps a shared memory of hard and soft user preferences drawn from plain speech. It reshapes on-screen options to match those preferences and spots clashes, suggesting backtracking while logging dead ends. In a 33-person movie-ticketing trial, bookings left fewer hard preferences unmet and broke stated preferences less often, though success rate and speed barely changed.
arxiv-2604-06334: Jangir investigates pairs of electrons and positrons produced from the vacuum by a strong electric field that oscillates, with a multi-pulse structure and variable delay between pulses. Values come from numerically solving the time-dependent Dirac equation. The analysis covers the momentum spread and total number density for different pulse counts and delays. The study demonstrates a distinctive time-domain multi-slit interference pattern in pair production probability as a function of inter-pulse delay.
arxiv-2604-06634: Kretkowski and eight colleagues build a deep-ultraviolet add-on for scanning electron microscopes, aiming toward orientation and work-function imaging. A UV-C light source, tilted and shifted by controls outside the vacuum chamber, shines on the sample during imaging. A polarizer tunes the light's field parts to steer electron emission from the surface in chosen directions. Modeling backs the expected boost in secondary electrons, and since no metal coating is needed, samples stay intact for later study.
arxiv-2604-06734: Zhang and three colleagues collect how humans actually solve problems by trial and error. Most trial-and-error AI methods lean on researcher-designed heuristics, and models lack detailed records of real human attempts. Their TEC platform records full user trajectories across trials plus reflections after error feedback, capturing 46 participants on 58 tasks for 5,370 trajectories across 41,229 webpages. Humans beat language models by a wide margin on accuracy, and the open platform and dataset aim to ground more capable trial-and-error AI.
arxiv-2604-07134: Dai and seven colleagues present LightCurveLynx, a flexible tool for forward modelling of time domain sky surveys from start to finish. Realistic fake surveys are needed to test analysis pipelines, tune survey plans, and run inference studies, yet building them end to end is a chore. LightCurveLynx builds fakes from real survey records, planned surveys, or user made mock plans. The authors test it by faking Type Ia supernovae to match the ZTF second data release, then compare fake and real samples in depth.
arxiv-2604-07234: Jeong and Pernice introduce the Random Subsequence Model, a model of spin-glass type counting embeddings of one string in another. They test a null model of independent strings and a planted model where the short string is drawn from the long one. In the dense regime, annealed and quenched free energies split at every density, hinting at a zero-temperature spin-glass phase. Hence random codes gain positive rate in the deletion channel for every deletion chance below one, the first such result at or above one half.
arxiv-2604-07334: Ali and Stettinger derive the BEF symplectic form, put forth in 2025 for nonlocal theories, straight from an L-infinity Lagrangian by the covariant phase space route. They nail down its exact link to the Barnich-Brandt form for theories with finite derivatives. When equations of motion are second order, the two forms agree, which explains the canonical corner term of general relativity in the BEF view. The BEF form also tracks generic corner terms and some boundary data, and the authors give a general Hamiltonian formula with worked examples.
arxiv-2604-07434: Kumar and three colleagues compute full tree-level bispectrum shapes for scalars at the cosmological collider and hunt for them in Planck data. Heavy particles decaying into inflaton quanta can leave oscillatory non-Gaussian marks, via single-, double-, and triple-exchange diagrams. The authors work out all three diagrams across the full range and find no sign of non-Gaussianity in Planck data. Tricks that beat steep falloff, including a scalar chemical potential trick, give only a 1.5-sigma hint.
arxiv-2604-07534: Padilla and Trillo give approximation orders for non-linear interpolation of data on sigma quasi-uniform grids, aimed at functions with isolated corner singularities. Their method joins ENO reconstruction with SR reconstruction. These methods cut error for such functions, aiding shock work and image work. The authors first prove what an algorithm spotting such singularities can do, then address the order reached by their method. For non-uniform grids with maximum node spacing below a key value, the optimal order is regained, as for smooth functions.
arxiv-2604-07634: Vasu and eight colleagues propose VSAS-Bench, a benchmark for streaming vision-language models that answer continuously from live video frames. Unlike offline tests, streaming scores also turn on proactiveness, response timeliness, and consistency over time. The benchmark packs over 18,000 dense annotations across varied domains and tasks, with standard synchronous and asynchronous protocols. Tests probe the accuracy-latency trade-off under memory length, access policy, and input resolution. Adapted conventional models beat recent streaming models without extra training; Qwen3-VL-4B tops Dispider by 3 percent asynchronously.
arxiv-2604-07834: Kim and five colleagues use language models to measure loneliness in caregivers and non-caregivers from social media text. They build an expert-designed rating scheme plus a typology for sorting causes of loneliness. A human-checked pipeline then applies GPT-4o, GPT-5-nano, and GPT-5 to assemble a high-quality Reddit corpus. The rating scheme reaches 76.09 percent accuracy for caregivers and about 80 percent for non-caregivers. The two groups differ a lot in which causes dominate their posts.
arxiv-2604-08134: Giraldo-Barreto and Holubec show how action-tied sensing creates cohesion in decision-driven matter. Living and built agents turn by tuning a utility score over finite actions. Rules based on pairwise sums over action-tied interaction zones give a general mechanism for clumping. That score splits into an average interaction score times the joined neighbor count. Maximizing it couples decisions to neighbor joining as a built-in result of the decision process. For alignment scores and turning actions, models reduce to a Vicsek variant when zones are action-independent.
arxiv-2604-08334: Vergani and four colleagues present mmid, a Python package for multi-modal merging and downstream healthcare analyses. mmid offers fusion and imputation, classification, time-to-event forecasts, and clustering under one front end, filling a gap in sequential merging and downstream healthcare analyses. mmid wraps decomposition, prediction, and clustering tools into one package, run by a single command and setup files, aiding reproducibility and transferability of studies with varied health data sources. The paper shows a demo on personalised cardiovascular risk scores.
arxiv-2604-08534: Zou and seven colleagues teach robots manipulation from first person human demos captured with smart glasses, no handheld controller needed. A stereo camera on the glasses records bare hand demos and later rides a six axis arm on the robot, reproducing human active vision. Object paths from demos feed a point cloud policy that predicts hand and head moves together, giving zero shot transfer across tasks with occlusion and across two robot platforms.
arxiv-2604-08834: Abdallah and three colleagues present BracketRank, a setup treating document resorting as a thinking driven contest format. Flexible grouping respects model context limits, and thinking boosted prompts demand step by step fit reasons. A bracket knockout structure with winner and loser tracks enables robust progress plus side by side work. On the BRIGHT thinking benchmark it reaches 26.56 nDCG@10, well ahead of RankGPT-4 and Rank-R1-14B rivals, and it also leads on TREC sets.
arxiv-2604-08934: Haraguchi and three colleagues trace crystal field and intraionic change in ilmenite salts and honeycomb zinc iridate, Mott blocks eyed as Kitaev liquid platforms. Iridium L3 edge x-ray scans show steady value change with element swap at the A site, and threefold bend grows with A site ionic radius. That explains drift from the ideal J equals one half state and opposed magnetism in cadmium iridate. Nearly the same spectral values in the two zinc compounds show lattice shape, not single ion traits, drives their unlike magnet ground states.
arxiv-2604-09034: Park and four colleagues recount the nextAI team's entry to the NeurIPS 2023 LLM Efficiency Challenge, which demanded fine-tuning a foundation model under tight limits. Their target was the LLaMA2 70 billion model, tuned on a single A100 40GB graphics card within 24 hours. A custom data methodology drove the effort, though the paper's focus stays on doing more with less hardware. The result was an efficiently tuned model that kept high accuracy across question answering benchmarks, showing large models can be optimized in resource-constrained settings.
arxiv-2604-09234: Chan tests whether the King Wen ordering of 64 I Ching hexagrams, an ancient pattern puzzling scholars for millennia, could aid neural network training. Checks against 100,000 random shuffles find four clear traits, including large jumps between steps and yang-balanced groups of four. Those traits echo teaching order ideas, motivating trials in learning rate changes, lesson ordering, and seed tests on two platforms. Results are all negative: the ordering degrades training at every amplitude and never beats seed variation, since its high variance upsets gradient training.
arxiv-2604-09434: Wang, Suarez, Bode, and Vinuesa show surrogate learning enables zero-shot control of turbulent wings. Turbulent boundary layers drive drag, yet control remains hard due to multiscale dynamics. Reinforcement learning beats state-of-the-art strategies in canonical flows, but realistic geometries suffer cost and poor transfer. The authors train policies in channel flows matched to wing statistics and deploy them onto a NACA4412 wing. Transferred policies cut drag by about 11 percent, versus about 9 percent for opposition control. Surrogate training improves exploration by about four orders of magnitude.
arxiv-2604-09834: Im and five co-authors investigate GJ 436 b, a hot Neptune with polar and eccentric orbits. They explore von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai migration from a distant companion behind the present-day orbit. Using about 20 years of radial velocity and Hipparcos-Gaia acceleration data, they constrain a potential companion. It must lie within about five and a half astronomical units for masses above about a twentieth of a Jupiter mass. Modeling favors sub-Jovian masses beyond about seven astronomical units, suggesting a substellar perturber. These constraints can guide future companion searches.
arxiv-2604-09934: Phuong Nguyen and Loc Nguyen solve an inverse initial-data problem for Navier-Stokes flow. The goal is finding initial speed and pressure from side readings, with the body force unknown. Time-changing the motion rule removes the unknown force, and a Legendre cut yields a coupled oval system for spread numbers. A shrinking map on an allowed set with a Carleman-weighted norm gives a fixed point for the reduced model, and shrink yields a settling Picard loop. A number method and fake-data tests show true rebuilds.
arxiv-2604-10034: Ku documents the first known perfect score by a language model on an officially disclosed Law School Admission Test. Controlled trials on eight reasoning models vary the prompt, shuffle choices, and sample several answers, with barely any effect. Removing the model's pre-answer thinking phase, however, cuts frontier accuracy by up to 8 percentage points, mainly in logical reasoning. Distilled models lag far behind despite producing full thinking traces. A pilot reward model trained on official explanations narrows the gap through best-of-five selection.
arxiv-2604-10334: Aziz and ten colleagues launch SIMPLER, a training scheme that uses H&E slides as a meaning anchor for SIM images. SIM images fresh tissue fast without staining, while it shows rich cell and gland structure. In training, SIM and H&E align step by step through rival, compare, and rebuild goals, so SIM vectors absorb H&E structure without losing their own style. One trained SIMPLER encoder serves tasks like multiple instance learning and shape grouping, beating models trained from scratch or with H&E training.
arxiv-2604-10734: Xu and five colleagues propose Self-Correcting RAG, a design tackling low context use and frequent hallucinations in retrieval-augmented generation for hard questions. Context choice becomes a multi-dimensional knapsack problem, maximizing information density and cutting redundancy under a strict token budget. On the output side, language-inference-guided Monte Carlo tree search explores thought paths and checks answer faithfulness using test-time compute. Tests on six multi-hop question-answering and fact-checking sets show stronger thought accuracy and fewer hallucinations than strong baselines.
arxiv-2604-10834: Camporese, Massacci, and Gong ask whether language models can act as auto labelers for technical security notes in human studies. Theme analysis of reasons is costly, since sound labeling needs several domain experts. Prompting four top models on LiveBench to spot nine security codes in weak code notes, they score outputs against human labelers with Cohen's Kappa. Clear gains appear only with rich code detail. Those gains vary by code and fall short of safely replacing a labeler. The authors urge more studies with more models and labeling tasks.
arxiv-2604-11134: Mourrat and Pillaud-Vivien present a counterexample to mean-field Langevin descent-ascent flow convergence. They consider payoff functions forming a double well in each coordinate, for which deterministic dynamics admits a limit cycle. When coupling between the two coordinates is strong and entropic regularization small, the mean-field dynamics stays close to this cyclic behaviour, and does not converge. The result shows that mean-field Langevin descent-ascent flow can fail to converge even under strong coupling and weak regularization, contradicting the convergence statement.
arxiv-2604-11334: Teng and eight colleagues detect depression from multiple modalities with a staged framework that pairs language-model summaries with clear reasoning. The pipeline screens for depression, classifies severity into five classes, and regresses a continuous score. At each stage, the language model writes step by step richer clinical notes to guide fusion of text, audio, and video features. All summaries merge into a concise plain report. Tests on E-DAIC and CMDC beat leading baselines on accuracy while staying clear.
arxiv-2604-11534: Jiang and Wei propose a circuit synthesis scheme for general quNit-quMit gates built from controlled-increment gates plus local gates. They show this pair forms a universal gate set for high-dimensional quantum computation. Any quNit-quMit gate needs at most O(n²) controlled-increment gates, the best known bound, and controlled gates need only 2, versus 2n in the previous scheme.
arxiv-2604-12134: Hennig asks whether several spinning, possibly charged black holes lined up on one axis can sit in lasting balance, with gravity held off by spin and electric repulsion. Using soliton techniques on the Einstein-Maxwell boundary problem, he derives the most general axis data such a setup allows, showing the potentials must be rational functions fixed by finitely many parameters. That turns a hard nonlinear equation hunt into checking a finite family of candidates.
arxiv-2604-12334: Lim and Choi study mixtures of Markov kernels that blend a baseline sampler with a Gibbs kernel from a partition of the state space. For the squared Frobenius goal they derive explicit trace formulas and a Cheeger-type rule marking optimal two-block splits, allowing fast approximation by majorization-minimization with geometric decay set by the spectral gap. For KL divergence, convexity bounds leave only the Gibbs part to choose. Curie-Weiss tests show well-chosen splits and mixing weights speed convergence in total variation.
arxiv-2604-12434: Abdessamed Qchohi and Simone Rossi study grokking, the late, sudden leap to broad skill in in-context learning. Transformers adapt from few examples, yet broad skill can arrive abruptly after long training. The team uses modular arithmetic tasks where a hidden linear rule must be guessed. Rough Bayesian tools track how forecast doubt shifts during training. Epistemic uncertainty falls fast exactly when the model groks. Doubt thus gives a label-free sign of broad skill. A plain Bayesian model links grokking time to doubt shifts.
arxiv-2604-12534: Victor David, Jérôme Delobelle, and Jean-Guy Mailly build a way to score how alike first-order logic arguments are. Likeness matters for grouping arguments and decoding enthymemes, arguments with unstated parts. Prior work stays in propositional logic, which lacks structured content. Their base is an extended set of rules. A four-level model covers predicates, literals, clauses, and formulae. Two model types add context weights, one sensitive to syntax via language models. Rules enforce the wanted traits throughout.
arxiv-2604-13234: Regaly, Frohlich, Kalup, and Kiss model narrow innermost rings of pebble- to sub-millimeter particles around Chiron, Chariklo, Quaoar, and Haumea over thousand-year timescales. In spherical models, solar radiation pressure pumps particle eccentricities until material falls onto the host, hitting lower-mass Chiron and Chariklo hardest. Adding the host's triaxial shape drives rapid apsidal precession that suppresses eccentricity growth. Strongly confined rings then persist for particles larger than about 7 to 40 micrometers, with widths near 10 kilometers for Chiron and Chariklo and 40 to 70 for Quaoar and Haumea.
arxiv-2604-13434: Bae determines the vertex-minor Ramsey number for four, showing it equals 11. It is the smallest count forcing every graph that large to contain the edgeless four-vertex graph as a vertex-minor. His proof classifies graphs on 10 and 11 vertices, using local complementation. At order 10, exactly six graphs avoid that edgeless graph as a minor. They form five local classes with orbit size 8,712. From those graphs he derives lower bounds beating the leading term up to nine, including at least 13 for five, and asks whether the five-case value is 15.
arxiv-2604-13634: Zhou and seven colleagues speed up language-model text generation with Calibrated Speculative Decoding. Standard checks wrongly reject some valid draft tokens, which wastes work. Their training-free method rescues those tokens instead of throwing them away. An Online Correction Memory recalls past patterns as rescue candidates. Semantic Consistency Gating then judges candidates by probability ratios, not exact token matches. Peak speedup reaches 2.33 times, accuracy stays intact, and hard reasoning tasks gain most.
arxiv-2604-13834: Chen, Cacciapuoti, and Caleffi rethink quantum routing. Standard routing assumes pathfinding must come first, a classical limit on how quantum a network can be. Their framework uses multipartite entanglement complementation to connect every non-adjacent pair in one hop, all at once. In plain terms, entanglement itself becomes the road, not a path to find. That redefines remoteness in the entanglement graph. Extended to inter-domain networks with a polynomial-time algorithm, it picks and parallelizes requests, skipping NP-complete path discovery, and cuts hops by up to 60 percent.
arxiv-2604-14134: Brunello and six colleagues give a closed formula for static post-Newtonian corrections to two-body motion at any odd order, once lower orders are known. Built in a correlation-function framework that exploits a twofold symmetry of the static sector, the formula reframes the factorization theorem. Applied at the seventh post-Newtonian order, it reproduces the diagrammatic result for two coalescing compact bodies, with contributions from seven-loop graphs.
arxiv-2604-14334: Balan and Feng test whether LLM chain-of-thought reasoning can filter tissue-composition confounders from saliency gene lists. A Mamba model on TCGA-BRCA data yields a top-50 saliency set, and DeepSeek-R1 checks candidates to produce a final 17-gene set. The raw 50-gene set trails a 5,000-gene baseline, while the LLM-filtered set beats it with 294 times fewer features. A faithfulness audit validates 6 of 17 selected genes as BRCA biomarkers, while 10 of 16 known input genes were missed. That gap shows targeted confounder removal can lift performance without comprehensive recall.
arxiv-2604-14534: Rosito and four colleagues propose an unsupervised multivariate system for athlete tracking, where small cohorts, mixed biomarker scales, rare repeat sampling, and missing injury ground truth limit standard models. The modular system works in the joint biomarker space, combining prep, safety screening, unsupervised grouping, and centroid-based reading. Profiles learned from amateur soccer players in one microcycle split mechanical damage from metabolic stress while keeping homeostatic states. Synthetic augmentation shows latent silent-risk patterns that single-variable tracking misses, with structure checks backing robustness.
arxiv-2604-14634: Lee and Son propose a massive-option method stretching candidate sets to one hundred options, sharply cutting chance. They test it on Korean spelling error checks, where models must find the one incorrect sentence in a large set. With fixed targets plus repeated resampling and shuffling, results stay stable, separating content failures from positional artifacts. Strong low-option performance often overstates competence, weakening under dense interference and revealing semantic confusion and early-option bias. Padding and length-matched tests point to option ranking, not context length, as the bottleneck.
arxiv-2604-14934: Liu and five others propose XQ-MEval, a semi-automatic dataset covering nine translation directions for benchmarking translation metrics. They inject MQM-defined errors into gold versions, filter them through native speakers, and merge errors into pseudo versions with set quality. Paired with sources and refs as triplets, these support metric assessment. Tests on nine metrics reveal mismatch between averaging and human judgment, giving the first empirical evidence of cross-lingual scoring bias. A scaling plan from XQ-MEval aligns score distributions across languages, improving multilingual metric fairness and reliability.
arxiv-2604-15034: Zhang and colleagues propose a shared protocol for AI agent systems that rewrite their own prompts, tools, and memory. Their design splits the job in two: one layer registers each changing part with clear state and versioned links, while a second layer handles proposals, checks, and commits. Past versions stay on record and can be restored, so change stays auditable. The team builds the scheme into a working multi-agent system that retrieves, sets up, and refines agents.
arxiv-2604-15134: Loginova and Keller build PIE-V, a tool for making mistake-aware first-person procedure videos for testing. Clean step procedures gain controlled, human-plausible slips from a psychology-informed error planner, plus a fix planner modeling recovery. A language-model writer rewrites steps so slips cascade cleanly, and a language-model judge checks sense and repairs failures. The goal is steady monitoring of real slips, which hands and subtle state changes often hide.
arxiv-2604-15334: Abraar and three colleagues pilot a hybrid learning platform that pairs video lectures with real-time conversational AI tutors. In a within-subjects trial with 58 learners averaging 21.4 years, everyone took the video-only version first, then the AI-augmented version. Post-test scores rose 8.3 points to 91.8 out of 100, and engagement time grew about 71 percent, offering early evidence that AI tutors can deepen video learning.
arxiv-2604-15734: Chen and Chen report bubble N68 in the G35 knot, a crash site of two gas clouds. Its half-ring holds 6 HII zones, 4 masers, 9 peaks, near 10 O/B stars, and 163 young stars. Two clouds, N68a and N68b, meet with wide bridge wisps and matched rims at 47 to 64 kilometers per second, marking a live crash. Star birth runs on pile-up collapse, blast-driven squeeze, and cloud crash, but the crash births big stars more than it lifts birth rates.
arxiv-2604-15834: Tavukoğlu, Olgun, and Azizi analyze rare decays of Lambda-b, Sigma-b, and Xi-b baryons into lighter baryons plus lepton pairs. They work in the Standard Model and in a Type III two-Higgs-doublet model. Using form factors from light-cone QCD, they compute decay widths, branching ratios, and lepton forward-backward asymmetries for muon and tau final states. Results are set against Standard Model predictions, lattice QCD, and existing data. The work also points to near-future tests at LHCb and Belle II.
arxiv-2604-15934: Svensson and seven colleagues present density response estimators for Monte Carlo simulations based on reweighting. Samples from a calm system estimate traits of a system pushed by an external harmonic potential, yielding linear and nonlinear response without simulating the pushed system. The method is shown on the uniform electron gas under warm dense matter and strongly coupled settings with path integral Monte Carlo. It extends to several pushes on different species and wavenumbers, opening access to cross-species response and the full quadratic response.
arxiv-2604-16134: Fischer and Roemelt extend earlier work on cavity-tuned spin effects. They move it into a relativistic Jahn-Teller setting, where light and matter couple strongly. Their system is one electron or one hole in a doubled molecular orbital of trigonal transition-metal complexes. It is shaped by vibration, spin-orbit coupling, and a quantized cavity field. Using a relativistic model plus an effective Hamiltonian method, they derive formulas for energy pairs and cavity-shifted g-factors in weak and strong coupling regimes.
arxiv-2604-16234: Le, Nguyen, and Nguyen present a two-stage, object-centred system for detecting exam cheating in exam-room images. Human invigilation is slow, costly, and error-prone at scale, while many AI monitors lack transparency or need tangled designs. Their system first locates students with YOLOv8n, then classifies each cropped region as normal or cheating with a fine-tuned RexNet-150 model. Trained on 273,897 samples from 10 sources, it reaches 0.95 accuracy, beating a baseline of 0.82.
arxiv-2604-16734: Kim and Bae propose a sequential input squeeze tool holding a fixed memory budget during prefill. Multimodal models store growing vision token caches, making memory a central choke as visual pictures richen. Old compression waits until all inputs are done, leaving peak memory high during prefill. Their structure-aware key-value cache compression runs during prefill, using shape patterns and overlap. Peak memory falls a lot with only minimal generative performance loss, for usable lean inference.
arxiv-2604-16834: Njungle, Jahns and Kinsy develop tuned recipes for batched HE-friendly neural networks. HE computes directly on encrypted data, but batch processing has lagged behind single-image inference. A pipeline architecture maximizes resource efficiency across batch sizes. On ResNet-20 with a batch of 512 encrypted images, amortized inference takes eight point eight six seconds per image with ninety-eight point nine six gigabytes peak memory. That is one point seven eight times faster and three point seven four times more memory-efficient than the leading design.
arxiv-2604-17534: Lopez and Clowes report a giant ring-like structure on the sky, an ultra-large-scale arrangement of galaxies at redshift around 0.8 in the same field as the earlier Giant Arc and Big Ring. The ring was predicted from a northern filament that looked poised to join the Arc, and new data now support its reality. Two overlapping versions differ only on the left-hand path, one matching the predicted ellipse and one tracing a nearly circular outline. The ring mixes a thin filamentary north with a clustered, ambiguous south.
arxiv-2604-17634: de la Fuente and four colleagues explore adding reconfigurable intelligent surfaces to cell-free massive MIMO networks in the FR1 and FR3 bands. Their framework analyzes RIS-assisted systems under propagation, accounting for frequency traits. A pairing algorithm assigns each surface to one user by line-of-sight links to tune phase shifts. The model uses Ricean fading channels and partial-MMSE combining. Results show this strategy lifts spectral efficiency above random or exhaustive setups, with moderate surface counts, while pilot needs can offset gains at high surface density.
arxiv-2604-17734: Wu and five colleagues propose a score-based cleaning framework for cryo-EM that recovers particle signals from the clean-data score while keeping shape information. A guided variant adds target guidance to steady learning under weak, unclear signals. Rather than boosting particle-like signals, it cuts patterned slow background, aiding particle-background split for later analysis. Tests on several cryo-EM sets show better particle picking and more structure-matching 3D rebuilds.
arxiv-2604-17834: Jie Liu and two colleagues build AsyncSparse, two sparse matrix multiplication kernels using new GPU features. One covers structured sparsity with a pipeline that moves data while math runs; the other splits row windows across blocks to balance uneven sparsity. On SuiteSparse matrices the uneven kernel runs 1.47 times faster than AccSpMM and 6.24 times faster than cuSPARSE, while the structured kernel speeds Qwen2.5-7B prefill 2.66 times at 90 percent block sparsity with 64,000 tokens.
arxiv-2604-18334: Shah, Habib, Hussain, Ghafoor, and Bangash study how reliable AI bots are inside GitHub Actions workflows. From 61,837 runs across 2,355 repositories, all triggered by pull requests from five bots, Copilot and Codex post the highest success rates at about 93 and about 94 percent. More frequent bot contributions correlate with lower success at the repository level. A taxonomy of 13 failure categories across 3,067 failed bot pull requests shows a drift from functional to non-functional failures over time, though not significantly.
arxiv-2604-18534: Kadets and Ribeiro present results on the weak minimizing property for infinite-dimensional separable Banach pairs. A pair has this property when every bounded linear operator with a non-weakly null minimizing sequence attains its norm minimum on the unit sphere. They show such a pair forces the domain space to be reflexive. If the domain is reflexive and the codomain holds no isomorphic copies of it, the pair has the property. If the codomain does contain such a copy, an equivalent norm on the codomain breaks the property.
arxiv-2604-18634: Ferrà Marcús and five colleagues use Mapper, boosted with new numeric scores, to weigh outer- versus inner-layer pacing in pigs with pacing-driven heart weakness. They study four blood-flow measures from an earlier trial, scoring each Mapper graph for self-links, spread, and evenness. Pacing from base zones differs sharply from mid or tip pacing, with base zones at 0.57 on the self-link score, above the other zones.
